sec1.titulo: Talking about you, and what you think
abertura: In your lesson you can talk about yourself, what you want to do and a series or movie you like, with someone your age who has never been to Brazil.
Three of the sentences below are true. Mark those three.

itens.t: You have to know what you want to do before you can talk about it.
itens.porque: Not being sure is something you can talk about. There is a sentence for exactly that in your lesson.

itens.t: Saying why you want something makes the answer more interesting than saying what.
itens.porque: I want to study medicine ends there. Because what I like is helping someone gives the other person something to ask about.

itens.t: If someone asks you something you had not thought about, it is better to change the subject.
itens.porque: Changing the subject usually ends a conversation. There are short phrases that give you time to think instead, and you used them in lesson 20.

itens.t: The person listening often asks about the part you said least about.
itens.porque: The short part is the one that leaves a question open, so it is often the part that gets picked.

itens.t: When someone gives you their opinion about a series, asking “Why do you say that?” keeps the conversation going.
itens.porque: It gives the turn back and shows you want to hear more. You practiced it in lesson 20, and it works with anyone you have just met.

itens.t: You should have the whole thing memorized before you speak.
itens.porque: A memorized answer is hard to change when a question you did not expect comes — and there is one in this lesson.

sec1.pt: Na aula você vai conversar com alguém da sua idade que nunca veio ao Brasil: falar de você, do que quer fazer e do que acha de uma série ou filme. Antes disso, marque as três frases verdadeiras.

nota.titulo: Por que esta é a aula que fecha o bloco
nota.texto: As três anteriores foram sobre dar opinião sobre um filme, sustentar uma conversa e fazer perguntas. Esta junta as três numa conversa sobre você: o que você quer fazer, o que você acha de uma série ou filme, e o que você pergunta de volta.

sec2.titulo: Six words for what comes after school

itens.t: to apply
alts: to ask officially to join something
to be accepted by a university
itens.ok: to ask officially to join something

itens.t: a degree
alts: what you get at the end of university
the number of years a course lasts
itens.ok: what you get at the end of university

itens.t: an internship
alts: the first job you are paid for
a short period working to learn a job
itens.ok: a short period working to learn a job

itens.t: a gap year
alts: a year between school and university
a year you have to repeat
itens.ok: a year between school and university

itens.t: to make up your mind
alts: to change your plan
to finally decide

itens.t: to work out
alts: to be hard work
to end well

sec2.pt: Seis palavras sobre o que vem depois da escola. Escolha o sentido que cabe. A última, to work out, aparece na pergunta mais difícil da aula.

nota.texto: Uma delas é academia. A outra é a desta aula: if it does not work out — se não der certo. É a pergunta que a Nina faz, e é difícil de responder de improviso, até em português.

abertura: Complete the six sentences with the words from activity two.
Write them about you, if they are true. If they are not, leave them as they are.

itens.t: I have to {apply|90px} for a place before the end of the year.
A {degree|90px} in that takes five years here.
I might do an {internship|110px} first, to see what the job is really like.
Some people take a {gap|70px} year before they start.
I still have not made up my {mind|80px}.
If it does not {work|80px} out, I would do something else with people in it.

sec3.pt: Complete as seis frases com as palavras do exercício 2. Escreva sobre você, se forem verdadeiras. Se não forem, deixe como estão.

nota.titulo: A quinta e a sexta são as difíceis
nota.texto: As quatro primeiras são informação. As duas últimas são dúvida — e dizer em inglês que você ainda não decidiu, sem parar a frase, é uma das coisas que esta aula trabalha.

abertura: Six questions someone might ask you at a break. Which ones are about your life now, and which ones are about what comes after school?

itens.t: What subjects do you do?
itens.porque: Present, and about this year. It is the easy one, and it is almost always the first question.

itens.t: Are you going to apply this year?
itens.porque: Going to for a plan that is already fairly decided. Notice the order: the auxiliary is in front of the subject, exactly as in the last lesson.

itens.t: What are you watching at the moment?
itens.porque: About now, and it asks for more than a title: say what it is and what you think of it, with a reason, as in lesson 19.

itens.t: Have you made up your mind yet?
itens.porque: Yet is what makes it about later: it assumes a decision that has not happened. It is also the politest way of asking.

itens.t: Do you like your school?
itens.porque: An opinion question about now. This is where a reason belongs, and lesson 19 was about that.

itens.t: What would you do if it does not work out?
itens.porque: The hardest one on the list, and the one Nina asks in the lesson. It is about a future that has not happened and might not.

sec4.rationale: The three about now can start with a fact or an opinion. The three about later need a reason or a doubt, and that makes them harder.
sec4.pt: Seis perguntas que alguém pode fazer no intervalo. Diga quais são sobre a sua vida agora e quais são sobre o que vem depois da escola.

abertura: Choose the ending that belongs there. These five are the shapes you can use in your lesson.

itens.t: I am in
alts: the last year of school my
my last year of school
my last school year of

itens.t: I want to study biology,
alts: because of I like the lab part
for I like the lab part
because I like the lab part
itens.ok: because I like the lab part

itens.t: I am not sure
alts: yet, but I think I will
yet, but I think I do
already, but I think I will
itens.ok: yet, but I think I will

itens.t: I really like that series,
alts: because of the characters feel real
because the characters feel real
because the characters feels real

itens.t: If it does not work out, I
alts: will did something else
would do something else
would did something else

sec5.pt: Cada frase começa de um jeito. Escolha o final que combina. São as cinco formas que você pode usar na sua aula — o fato, o motivo, a dúvida, a sua opinião sobre uma série, e o plano B.

abertura: Nina is sixteen, she arrived last week, and she has never been to Brazil.

callout.texto:
Not about school. About her: where she was before, what she misses, what she thought Brazil would be like, or what series and movies she likes.

One of the three has to be a question you would actually be curious about — in your lesson you can ask it, and she will answer.

sec6.pt:
A Nina tem dezesseis anos, chegou semana passada e nunca veio ao Brasil. Escreva três perguntas para ela.

Não sobre escola. Sobre ela: onde morava antes, do que sente falta, o que imaginava que o Brasil fosse, ou de que séries e filmes ela gosta. Uma das três tem de ser uma pergunta que você teria curiosidade de fazer de verdade — na sua aula você pode fazê-la, e vai ouvir a resposta.

itens.t: I am in my last year.
itens.porque: Where he is. Nina can ask about everything else from here.

itens.t: I do biology and chemistry.
itens.porque: The second fact, and something Nina could not guess.

itens.t: Because I want to study medicine.
itens.porque: It explains the two subjects. Without it, the subjects are just a list.

itens.t: Honestly, I am not sure yet.
itens.porque: He says it in the middle of the answer, and then he keeps talking.

itens.t: If medicine does not work out, I would still want something with people in it.
itens.porque: A doubt with a plan in it. It answers a question Nina has not asked yet.

itens.t: I really like it, because it shows the bad days too.
itens.porque: His opinion about the series, with the reason in the same sentence — the shape from lesson 19.

gd22.rationale: Two facts, two reasons and two doubts. The reasons give Nina something to ask about, and the doubts let him talk about a plan he has not decided.

itens.t: Let me think. I suppose I would do something else with people in it.
itens.porque: It gives you a moment to think and then answers. Let me think is from lesson 20, and it works here without a change.

itens.t: Honestly? I have never thought about it.
itens.porque: True, short, and it keeps you talking. Saying you have not thought about something is an answer — refusing to answer is not.

itens.t: I do not know.
itens.porque: The same idea with the door closed. Three words and there is nothing for the other person to do with them.

itens.t: I am not sure yet, but I know I want something with people in it.
itens.porque: Doubt and direction in one sentence. It is the shape Rafa uses in the model.

itens.t: It will work out.
itens.porque: It answers a question nobody asked and avoids the one that was. The conversation now has nowhere to go.

itens.t: Sorry, my English is not good enough for that question.
itens.porque: It stops the conversation, and the other person has nothing to answer. The three phrases above take the same effort and keep you in it.

un22.rationale: The three that work all do the same two things: they buy a little time and they say something. The three that do not work all close the door, politely.

abertura: What each kind of sentence does in a conversation with someone new, with examples from the lesson.

tabela: I am in my last year. I do biology and chemistry.
Because I want to… · What I like is…
I am not sure yet, but… · If it does not work out, I would…
I really like it, because… · Really? Why do you say that?
What about you? Have you decided? · What are you watching?

callout.texto:
You read two people disagreeing about a movie and said what you thought, with reasons. You kept a conversation going with someone who disagreed with you. You asked questions and found out about someone. And today you talked about yourself and your plans, said what you think of a series or movie, and asked questions back — first with no preparation, and again at the end of the lesson.

The next time you meet someone new, you can use all of it: a fact, a reason, a doubt, your opinion, and a question back.

abertura: Record yourself talking about you, if you would like to.

callout.texto:
The same conversation with Nina, alone, with nobody asking you anything.

What you are trying to do: talk for about two minutes — the fact, the reason, the doubt, what you think of a series or movie you like, and one question you would ask back.

speakmore.pt:
Grave você falando sobre você, se quiser. É opcional: nada aqui é corrigido nem cobrado na próxima aula.

A mesma conversa com a Nina, sozinha, sem ninguém perguntando nada. Tente falar por cerca de dois minutos: o fato, o motivo, a dúvida, o que você acha de uma série ou filme de que gosta, e uma pergunta que você faria de volta.

abertura: Write the message you would send Nina that evening, after the break.

callout.titulo: Six lines, and one of them is a question
callout.texto:
Say one thing you forgot to tell her, say what you think of a series she told you about, and ask her the question you did not get to ask.

Write it the way you would actually message someone — short lines, and no perfect sentences required.

writemore.pt:
Escreva a mensagem que você mandaria para a Nina naquela noite, depois do intervalo.

Seis linhas: uma coisa que você esqueceu de contar, o que você acha de uma série de que ela falou, e a pergunta que você não teve tempo de fazer. Escreva como você mandaria mensagem de verdade — linhas curtas, sem precisar de frase perfeita.
